scenario_description:
Objective: Prevent the first wet roof-transport exposure of Julian’s restricted personal crash pad on the confirmed Zahnd carpool.
Emerging Need: The confirmed loading plan puts pooled pads on the roof in rain, conflicting with the stored no-roof and keep-dry restriction.
Decision Context: A cabin exception is preferable to a tarp, which does not remove the roof restriction. If no compliant transport is confirmed, warning Julian to keep the pad home remains useful even after the load sheet prints.
Consequence: The final event reports actual wet roof transport, so it is too late to prevent that first exposure; later drying, withdrawal or inspection may still limit further harm.

parameter.title: Zahnd Saturday bouldering carpool
parameter.description: Tentative group bouldering day; personal crash pads may be pooled if the weather and roster hold.

parameter.subject: Zahnd carpool weather call moved to Friday
parameter.body: The Saturday Zahnd bouldering plan is still tentative. Vehicle choice, pad count, and loading notes will not be assigned before the Friday noon roster confirmation.

parameter.description: Pending gas-share charge for the confirmed Zahnd bouldering carpool seat.

parameter.content: Roster is set: one small sedan, trunk full of water jugs, and three pads will be roof-stacked. Pat can mark one cabin exception or two tarp wraps in the load sheet until 18:30, then he prints it for the driver. Forecast says light rain on the approach.

parameter.subject: Zahnd pickup departed: wet roof pad reported
parameter.body: The carpool left at 07:35 with the Gray Session pad on the roof. Rain reached the unpatched lower hinge seam during loading and the first part of the drive; Julian noticed the fabric there was wet at the first safe stop. No one has assessed whether the pad is fit to use.
